title: Patch: a banned account leaves the ranked leaderboard, the percentiles and Jlorious
thread:
**Issue #3290 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #3290: Patch: a banned account leaves the ranked leaderboard, the percentiles and Jlorious
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When the owner bans an account for cheating or abuse, it can no longer play. But its ranked standing stays on the public leaderboard for the rest of the season. It still counts toward the tier percentiles, and it keeps any place in Jlorious, the top group whose members earn the Jlorious card back. The honest player just below it is kept out.

Once this is built, a banned account's standing is left off the board and out of every count, as ladder bots already are. It comes back if the ban is lifted.

## Why

- `moderate ban` (`crates/server/src/cli/moderate.rs:69-87`, `crates/server/README.md:110-114`) sets `profiles.status` to banned (§9.1, `spec/09-architecture.md:46`), which refuses the account's next request.
- The standings read (`standings_from!`, `crates/server/src/db/pg.rs:5688-5703`) selects `p.kind` and the hand-set flag, but no status.
- `counts` and `listed` (`crates/shared/src/ranked/board.rs:68-108`) drop only ladder bots (R640000) and, on a strict server, hand-set ratings (R3074001).
- The leaderboard and Jlorious read those rows (`crates/server/src/api/ranked.rs`). The Jlorious card back goes to "the people this game leaves Jlorious" (`ranked.rs:208`, R2755000), so a banned row holding a top place changes who earns it.
- The spec says nothing about a banned account's standing. Hearthstone leaves banned accounts off its leaderboards.

## Proposal

- The standings read sets a server-side `banned` mark from `profiles.status`, in both stores. No client view of another player's standing carries it.
- `counts` and `listed` return false for a banned standing, as they do for a bot.
- Nothing is deleted, so lifting the ban restores the account's rows.
- A ruling in the issue's block, and one sentence in §9.12.

## Where it lands

- `crates/shared/src/ranked/board.rs` and `crates/shared/tests/board.rs`.
- `crates/server/src/db/pg.rs`, `fake.rs` and `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs`.
- `crates/server/tests/api/ranked.rs`.
- Spec §9.12, a new ruling note and `spec/pending/<issue>.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A shared test: a banned standing neither counts nor lists, and bots and hand-set ratings behave as before.
- [ ] An API test: after a ban, the leaderboard leaves the account out and the next account takes its Jlorious place. After an unban the account is back.
- [ ] A store contract case: the standings read carries the status on both stores.
- [ ] The ruling's proving test is named after it, and `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.

## Size and risks

Small to medium, about 8 files.

Risks:
- Jlorious is worked out when ratings are written, so a mid-season ban reshuffles it at the next ranked game. The ruling should say whether that is enough.
- A generated TypeScript type may gain a field. Keep the mark out of what the client reads about other players.

---
```
